To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) InsP3-stimulation of Ca2+ stores is quantal in Ca2+-free media containing either EGTA or the fast Ca2+ chelator BAPTA, and 2) quantal responses are not due to regulatory effects of cytoplasmic Ca2+ on the InsP3 receptor.
the quantal pattern observed at 37 degreesC is not a consequence of the Ca2+ regulation, and that quantal pattern does not reverse at 2degreesC.
quantal responses to inositole 1,4-5 trisphosphate are non-enzymatic and non-reversible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the quantal pattern exhibited by the InsP3 receptor.
the regulation of the intracellular Ca(2+ )stores of hepatocytes by inositol 4,5-bisphosphate (IP(4)) and inositol 3,4,5,6-tetrakisphosphate (IP6).
the mechanisms by which inositol 4,5-triphosphate (InsP(3)) mobilizes Ca(2+) from intracellular stores.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quantal response to InsP3 is due to a change in the affinity of InsP3 binding to the InsP3 receptor.
quantal Ca2(+)-mobilizing effects of InsP(3) are not a consequence either of Ca(2+) regulation of InsP( 3) receptors, or of enzyme-mediated regulation of InsP3 receptors.

quantal responses to inositols are not a consequence either of the regulation of inosital 1,4-5-triphosphate receptors by cytosolic free Ca2+ or by ATP, but that they are a consequence of the kinetics of the inositol 3-4-5-trisphophate receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the InsP3 receptor has two distinct modes of regulation: a slow, enzyme-mediated mode that is sensitive to Ca2+ and ATP, and an immediate mode of Ca2+ gating that is independent of ATP.
the quantal responses to inositols are not a consequence, but a property of the inositol trisphosphate receptor.
InsP3 receptors do not have an allosteric binding site for Ca2+.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the quantal pattern is an inherent characteristic of the InsP(3) receptor, and that the quantal responses to inositols are not a consequence, or a reflection, of the effects of Ca(2+) on the inositol 3-phosphate receptor.
the quantal pattern in Ca2+ release is a result of the InsP(3) receptors' ability to be activated by InsP(3).
quantal release is not an artifact of Ca2+ buffering.
